label: conj:p-vs-np-qou
title: P vs NP in the QOU: classical-limit separation of BQP-width classes
html:
Conjecture (q-complexity separation). Let \varepsilon be the Reeb infinitesimal (Reeb infinitesimal) and q = 1 + \varepsilon the associated substrate parameter. Let \mathrm{BQP}_q denote the class of decision problems solvable in polynomial time on a q-deformed computational substrate (a topological quantum computer whose anyonic model is the R-matrix of \mathbf{C}_q). Then

\mathbf{P} \neq \mathbf{NP}

in classical complexity theory. This separation is recovered as the standard part \mathrm{st}_{\varepsilon \to 0} of the strict inclusion

\mathbf{P} \subsetneq \mathrm{BQP}_q \qquad (\text{for every } \varepsilon > 0 \text{ in } \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon)).

The Reeb period \Omega_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-1} (surreal rate calculus) measures the natural time budget of a computation on the q-substrate. A polynomial-time q-algorithm executes \mathrm{poly}(n) \cdot \Omega_q^{O(1)} elementary skein moves in a Reeb period, a transfinite quantity in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon) \subset \mathbf{No}. A polynomial-time classical algorithm executes at most \mathrm{poly}(n) elementary moves in the same period—a standard-real quantity.

The conjecture asserts that the classical-limit functor (\varepsilon \to 0, equivalent to applying the standard-part map to the q-substrate computation; see calculus up to \varepsilon) collapses the transfinite Reeb budget to a bounded finite budget, losing the q-advantage. The standard part of \mathrm{BQP}_q strictly exceeds \mathbf{P} only if NP-complete problems exist whose q-algorithms do not admit a convergent \varepsilon \to 0 expansion.

We offer a heuristic argument. The mass-gap dissipation \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3 bounds the energy the substrate can absorb per computational step. An NP-complete search with 2^n witnesses requires 2^n classical elementary tests. On the q-substrate, the search is a single Reeb-flow holonomy, which takes Reeb time \asymp \Omega_q = \varepsilon^{-1}. For the q-algorithm to classically accelerate to polynomial time as \varepsilon \to 0, each elementary test must be absorbed in mass-gap energy \Delta_q, with classical budget 2^n \cdot \Delta_q \asymp 2^n \cdot \varepsilon^3 per computation. The available q-algorithm cost is the per-step efficiency dressed by the Reeb period: 2^n \cdot \delta_n^2 \cdot \Omega_q \asymp 2^n \cdot \varepsilon^{-1}. By surreal squeeze, the cost strictly exceeds the budget (equivalently \ordw(\text{cost}) = 1 > -3 = \ordw(\text{budget})). The q-algorithm cannot be classically compressed. The 2^n-fold speedup cannot fit inside the classical mass-gap budget.

This conjecture is speculative. It is formulated in the Reeb--surreal framework but lacks a Lean formalisation. A formal proof would reduce the q-to-classical compression obstruction to the structural non-existence of a \mathrm{BQP}_q \to \mathbf{P} functor, consistent with the Freedman--Kitaev--Larsen--Wang topological model at q-generic.

This surreal-squeeze route is one of two independent attacks on the same separation. The obstruction-class route (\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} at non-torsion q) instead states the separation as non-vanishing of the resolution-tree residue \mathrm{res}_{\mathcal{R}}(\chi(A)) \neq 0 at q_0. The two carriers share the conclusion \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} but neither is derived from the other; both remain open.

See Surreal bound for P vs NP for the squeeze-inequality statement implied by this conjecture.
